correctionWave2.why: MASTER independently confirmed 2/3 PASS at the wave-1 hash against this writer's then-current implementation: the grammar test failed because a counterfeit PolicyStatement built directly on PolicyStatement.prototype (carrying a hostile own-property `id` getter, no real private brand state) was silently admitted by the constructor's prior `Array.isArray(statements) && statements.every(isExactly(..., PolicyStatement))` check, which tests prototype identity only and never a genuine private-field brand. The test writer's replan added two adversarial assertions to the grammar test: (1) that same counterfeit statement must be refused by the constructor with a TypeError before its hostile `id` getter ever runs, and (2) a sparse (holed) statements array must likewise be refused with a TypeError rather than silently densified. Both required a source-side fix in the allowed src/application/policy-candidate-resolver.mjs, not a further test correction, since the counterfeit-admission gap was a genuine implementation defect.
correctionWave2.redAtWave2: 2/3 PASS against this writer's pre-fix implementation, confirmed independently by MASTER before this writer's second pass: the grammar test failed exactly at the new counterfeit-admission assertion (`Missing expected exception: a counterfeit PolicyStatement lacking private brand state must be refused with a TypeError`); the integration and determinism tests remained GREEN, unaffected.
correctionWave2.greenAtWave2: 3/3 PASS after this writer added a captured-private-getter brand check (`PolicyStatement.prototype`'s `effect` getter, called on each candidate statement — `effect` rather than `id` because the adversarial fixture overrides `id` specifically) and a dense-array admission check (`Array.isArray`, exact `Array.prototype`, no hole, no property beside its indices) to the `PolicyCandidateResolver` constructor, both evaluated and failing closed with a `TypeError` before any statement's own-property getter is ever reached. All other resolver semantics (targetActor/targetAction/targetResourceType/condition/enabled matching, the v2 candidate shape, purity, determinism, the existing PolicyRequest brand check) are unchanged.

goal: Add PolicyCandidateResolver, a frozen class holding a fixed array of genuine PolicyStatement rows, exposing one synchronous method candidatesFor(request) that: (a) refuses a non-genuine PolicyRequest with a TypeError before any of its own-property getters run (proven against a hostile lookalike carrying a getter-trapped `action`); (b) maps each statement to the exact ordinary 5-key v2 candidate shape {policyId, effect, applies, priority, layer} already accepted unchanged by AuthorizationEvaluator/PolicyDecisionPoint; (c) computes applies from statement.enabled, exact targetAction/targetResourceType equality, a targetActor grammar admitting only optional tenantId/actorId string keys (any other key fails closed), and an empty-object-only unconditional condition (any non-empty condition fails closed, never evaluated, never thrown); (d) is deterministic, order-independent, and mutates neither the input statements array, any PolicyStatement, nor the PolicyRequest passed in.
nonGoals: no change to any existing public contract (PolicyStatement, PolicyRequest, PolicyDecision, AuthorizationEvaluator, PolicyDecisionPoint)
no combining algorithm or deny-overrides execution — that stays in AuthorizationEvaluator/PolicyDecisionPoint
no condition evaluator beyond the empty-object unconditional case
no persistence, statement store, cache, batch or decision-log
no PEP, HTTP or UI surface
no version bump, CI/config change, dependency change, commit, push, PR, full npm test/check, release or deploy
no Agent/child/background worker; direct work only
